title: Minimax Precision When Each Unit Has One Unknown Interfering Partner within a Cluster

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the full-record hidden-link rate B^2 min{1,D^2/n}, a clipped UNITE attainer, the consistency boundary and supplied-link comparison; the math review passed and the cited equation was verified. The independent validity gate confirmed subfield novelty below the field floor, with score ceiling 7.1 below 7.4 and no bounded improvement directive; formalization was not launched, so no Lean theorem is claimed. Preserve the omitted accepted known-graph comparator, non-novel superset inclusion transfer and stale deferred-source prose; fixed-D constants remain new research rather than a bounded repair.
tldr: A single fair-Bernoulli experiment with fixed potential outcomes has minimax mean-square precision of order \(B^2\min\{1,D^2/n\}\) when each response has one unknown partner inside a known cluster of size \(D\). The same frontier holds for the containing bounded noiseless equal-cluster first-order additive specialization of UNITE. The inherited clipped score attains it in linear time, and a legal finite-prior converse applies to every nonlinear or randomized rule using the entire labeled record. Uniform consistency holds exactly when \(D=o(\sqrt n)\); supplied links in the degree-one model instead give risk of order \(B^2/n\). Exact fixed-cluster leading constants remain a separate efficiency question.
gap: UNITE supplies the candidate-neighborhood score and design variance guarantees. Its first-order additive framework does not state an all-estimator minimax frontier for fixed hidden within-cluster bijections. Available lower-bound templates preserve the full record but do not by themselves verify this narrower frontier.
fill: An explicit \(r(n,D)\), an original-record algorithm, and a matching converse determine which candidate-cluster sizes support uniform precision. The existing UNITE estimator and its public implementation are the concrete consumer; the bijection model is a prospective use case, not a claim about their verified deployments.
